ScienceClaw epilepsy research system · study summary

Virtual brain twins for treatment choice: study-002

Using Wang et al. 2025 virtual brain twin data (simulated Patients 1 and 2, VBT_INS_Stimulation), can a qualified virtual-brain pipeline recover the epileptogenic zone of a held-out virtual patient from its SEEG, and which virtual intervention (resection/ablation of the estimated zone or electrical stimulation) most reduces simulated seizure spread, judged against the hidden ground truth?

Study study-002Release rel-f02dbe461251 Protocol v1 (A0001) + amendments A0012, A0015Run 2026-11-01 13:03 – 17:22 UTC Status: ✓ completed
Exploratory results on a virtual patient. The inversion model did not pass its qualification benchmark (v2 A0037, v3 A0040), so the onset-zone estimates and the treatment ranking below are exploratory. Nothing here is a clinical recommendation.

For clinicians

  • We built a virtual brain twin of Wang et al.'s virtual Patient 2 (162-region connectome, 205 SEEG contacts) and tested resection/ablation and electrical stimulation in silico before any (virtual) intervention.
  • Exploratory result: removing the model's estimated onset + spread regions reduced the number of seizing regions most (median -3; all seizures stopped in 42% of model samples). Sustained-current SEEG stimulation helped a little; the paper's 50 Hz pulse train did not.
  • Against the sealed ground truth the model failed: the true onset region (Left-F1-lateral-prefrontal) was not among the estimated regions, and the treatment ranking could not be confirmed. The value shown here is the honest negative result and a clear path to fix it.

For engineers

  • Seven agent roles worked through a deterministic controller: every task admitted against a frozen profile, every artifact gated by another role, truth sealed in a vault until predictions were frozen (freeze hash 1fcf288a…).
  • Two inversion models were tried and both failed qualification: v2 (≈520 parameters, R-hat up to 4.7) and v3 (68 parameters, Pathfinder modes spread ≈50 nats). Root cause: the 2D fitting model cannot reproduce data generated by the richer 6D model.
  • Treatments were simulated with the paper's full TVB SpatEpiStim model (reproduces the package bit for bit), on the GCP VM and locally, with paired baselines.

2 · Workflow and agent history

Same controller-governed workflow as study-001, run on the release that includes study-001's lessons (benchmark-first modeling, sealed outcome files, larger budgets). Two protocol amendments were approved by the user: cloud compute (A0012) and a parallel schedule to meet a noon deadline (A0015).

4 · Virtual-brain modeling

Strategy (as in Wang et al. 2025): infer each region's excitability x0 with a reduced 2D Epileptor network in Stan, then simulate treatments with the full stimulation model in TVB. A pipeline must first recover a planted onset zone on synthetic data (benchmark) before its patient estimates count.

5 · Simulation: virtual brain, stimulation and treatments

R4 simulated every prespecified candidate on each of the 12 best full-window MAP solutions with a paired no-treatment baseline (TVB SpatEpiStim, 0.05 ms steps, 14.4 s horizon). Stimulation follows the paper: a bipolar SEEG contact pair, 50 Hz biphasic pulses, spatial weights from that contact's gain. The detailed R4 report is study-002-R4-simulations.html.

6 · Ground-truth check (R5, after the prediction freeze)

R5 opened the sealed configuration only after the predictions were frozen (freeze before reveal in the ledger), scored the frozen onset estimates, and re-ran R4's planned treatments plus an oracle (ablating the true onset zone) on the true virtual patient. Records: A0043-OutcomeEvaluation, A0044. Verdict: failed.

True onset zone

Left-F1-lateral-prefrontal (a single region; no propagation zone set). None of the four frozen estimates contained it (recall 0); the most frequent estimate was Right orbito-frontal cortex, the region with the strongest SEEG coverage.

Treatment ranking

On the true model in the region-level simulator the patient did not seize spontaneously, so no candidate, not even ablating the true onset zone, could show an effect. Rank concordance is undefined; in the full window all 9 predicted reductions had the wrong sign. The recorded seizure was stimulation-induced, so the next check is to simulate the observed stimulation protocol.

7 · Quality controls and limitations

Controls

  • Ground truth and the authors' notebooks/posteriors sealed (10 items) before modeling; revealed once, to R5, after the freeze.
  • Every model frozen with hashes before its benchmark; failures reported, not tuned away.
  • 5 repairs; 4 proposals refused by the controller.

Limitations

  • No qualified inversion model: onset estimates and treatment ranking are exploratory.
  • Region-level (not neural-field) simulation; 12 of 24 samples in the full window; post window uninformative (no baseline seizures).
  • Simulated top channels did not match the recording's (qualitative check failed).
  • Virtual patients from one study family; not a clinical result.
